title: Mexico City Will Open Free Medical Clinics in 600 Neighborhoods
author: Alejandro Cruz Flores
content:
_This article by[Alejandro Cruz
Flores](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Alejandro%20Cruz%20Flores)
originally appeared in the [November 22, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/11/22/capital/en-cdmx-
abriran-consultorios-medicos-gratuitos-en-600-colonias), Mexico's premier left
wing daily newspaper._

On **January 1, 2027** , the federal and Mexico City governments will launch a
strategy to bring health services to communities by setting up medical clinics
and laboratory facilities in **600 neighborhoods** of the capital.

Mexico City Mayor Clara Brugada Molina explained that the federal government
will provide the clinics, which will have doctors and free medicines, while
the city will be responsible for the laboratories, where tests of “all kinds”
will also be carried out free of charge.

The program is coordinated by **IMSS-Bienestar** and, the capital’s mayor
said, is the largest strategy for bringing health care into local communities,
although she did not specify in which districts these measures would be
carried out. Covering one-third of the capital’s neighborhoods, it will also
include emotional well-being clinics as part of the city government’s Vida
plena, corazón contento program.

> “Perhaps some people say: it is not necessary to be emotionally well. We
> think it is, that it is a right, and we will have **600 mental health
> professionals** caring for children, young people, women and men in the
> heart of the community.”

At an event where she handed out Hombres Bienestar pension cards, which
provide financial support of 3,000 pesos every two months to men aged 60 to 64
who reside in the city, Brugada Molina acknowledged that “we have few health
centers, (but) now we are going to multiply them, we are going to bring this
right to your doorstep” in the neighborhoods, districts and towns of the
nation’s capital.

Meanwhile, at Fray Nano Stadium in the Venustiano Carranza borough, the mayor
emphasized that Hombres Bienestar currently has 123,000 beneficiaries and is
expected to reach 200,000 next year.

She stressed that this initiative recognizes the contribution of those who
have dedicated their lives to the capital’s development and ensures they can
receive a pension before reaching the age set by the Mexican government for
access to the older adults’ pension. “No one has to wait until they are 65 to
receive a pension. In this great Mexico City, women and men receive a support
pension starting at age 60.”

Later, she attended Iztacalco Mayor Lourdes Paz’s activity report, where she
highlighted the importance of borough governments in strengthening the
transformation in the capital, and announced that Utopías would be built in
the Agrícola Oriental, Agrícola Pantitlán, Santa Anita and 2 de Octubre
neighborhoods, along with an expansion of the one already operating in
Magdalena Mixiuhca, which will be geared toward children.
